newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: RESEARCH ALERT-CT SMITH SAYS BUY LANKA BLUE CHIPS.
newsitem.headline: RESEARCH ALERT-CT SMITH SAYS BUY LANKA BLUE CHIPS.

text.p: Brokerage CT Smith said on Thursday it was putting buy recommendations on Sri Lankan blue chip conglomerates, finance and manufacturing stocks since they were expected to perform better this year.

The firm said in a research report that blue chip conglomerates John Keells Holdings and Hayleys, which are expected to post an average growth of about 24 percent in the financial year to March 31, 1998, were good buys at current levels.
Shares of John Keells and Hayleys were trading at 365 and 275 rupees, respectively, on Thursday.
"John Keells should be aided by strong performances in food and beverage, coupled with a much improved performance from tourism," the report said.
"Hayleys should post steady growth in earnings through its growing dominance in core business and consolidation in non-core areas," it added.
Hayleys core areas are activated carbon, rubber products, plantations, tourism and coir products.
The third conglomerate Aitken Spence, which has achieved dominance in tourism and cargo handling, offers an excellent long-term buying opportunity, the brokerage said.
Aitken Spence shares traded at 210 rupees on Thursday.
Development Finance Corporation (DFCC), was also recommended as a "long-term buy".
"Hurt by adverse economic conditions, DFCC's portfolio grew only 10 percent in the financial year to March 31, 1997, against a five year growth rate of 17 percent," said CT Smith.
"However, buoyed by an improving economic scenario, DFCC is poised for a strong recovery," it added.
The scrip was trading at 315 rupees on Thursday.
Sri Lanka's economy grew just 3.8 percent in 1996 compared to 5.5 percent in 1995, due to a severe drought which hit power supplies, industry and agriculture.

Tourism was affected after Liberation Tigers of Tamil Eelam rebels, who are fighting for a separate homeland for minority Tamils in Sri Lanka's north and east, bombed the Central Bank and a commuter train last year.
But the latest forecast from the Central Bank has gross domestic product (GDP) growing at least six percent in 1997.
The report said Sampath Bank, another finance blue chip, is expected to see profit growth of at least 20 percent in the year to December 31, 1997 on the back of Sri Lanka's economic recovery.
The share, which was trading at 81 rupees on Thursday, is recommended as a good "buy" at current levels, the report added.
